name: Severe Weather Event Reporter
what_it_holds: Automated severe-weather event analysis tool generating post-event reports (radar imagery, meteorological analysis, damage assessments) by integrating eight federal data sources including NOAA and NWS, tagged for NOAA's Storm Events Database.
why_useful: Storm Events Database (tornadoes, severe thunderstorms, floods, winter storms -- broader than just hurricanes) by county/date is a finer-grained US weather-shock source than HURDAT2 alone; this tool's multi-source integration could shortcut assembling a county-level severe-weather panel for market-level demand shocks.

why_all: Storm Events Database (tornadoes, severe thunderstorms, floods, winter storms -- broader than just hurricanes) by county/date is a finer-grained US weather-shock source than HURDAT2 alone; this tool's multi-source integration could shortcut assembling a county-level severe-weather panel for market-level demand shocks.

name: TheEconomist/big-mac-data
what_it_holds: Official Economist Big Mac Index source data and methodology, MIT licensed, 1748 stars, updated same day as our search (13 Sep 2026, actively maintained). Three committed files: big-mac-raw-index.csv, big-mac-adjusted-index.csv (GDP-adjusted), big-mac-full-index.csv, each carrying underlying local prices, exchange rates and implied-vs-actual PPP by country. Biannual since ~2000, ~70 countries incl. all ABNB's major regions (EU, UK, Japan, Australia, Mexico, Brazil, India). July 2022 methodology change archived in Releases so old vintage is recoverable.
why_useful: Direct, long-running, free PPP/affordability series by country -> usable as a cross-check on real (purchasing-power-adjusted) ADR moves and as an affordability proxy for inbound/outbound travel demand by region (gap #6 consumer spend / broader macro-consumer-spend theme, and general FX/PPP gap not separately numbered but explicitly requested by this theme). Also a clean point-in-time-able series since each release is dated and archived.
time_coverage: ~2000-present, semiannual (Jan/Jul), with July 2022 methodology break archived separately
size_hint: 3 CSVs, small (~tens of KB), full history
themes: FX and purchasing power: exchange-rate history (ECB, BIS, FRED), broad-dollar indices, PPP/Big Mac, tourist affordability indices, company FX-exposure tooling
wildcard: an FX and macro strategist who models translation effects an
why_all: Direct, long-running, free PPP/affordability series by country -> usable as a cross-check on real (purchasing-power-adjusted) ADR moves and as an affordability proxy for inbound/outbound travel demand by region (gap #6 consumer spend / broader macro-consumer-spend theme, and general FX/PPP gap not separately numbered but explicitly requested by this theme). Also a clean point-in-time-able series since each release is dated and archived.

Direct PPP/affordability cross-country series -- a standard proxy for real currency over/undervaluation that could feed a cross-border demand/affordability adjustment for ABNB's international nights and ADR mix (gap area: PPP/Big Mac in theme, tangential to gap 6/7 consumer strength by country).

A ready, standing measure of currency over/undervaluation by country -- a cheap cross-border 'purchasing power' signal that could feed into ADR-ex-FX translation checks and outbound-demand direction by region (does a currency look cheap enough to pull travelers in/out).

name: world-infrastructure-data-hub
what_it_holds: Daily-refreshed, GitHub-Actions-built static JSON API (countries.json, per-country files) covering retail gasoline/diesel/LPG prices (USD/L) for ~130 countries from the EU Weekly Oil Bulletin and World Bank Global Fuel Prices DB, plus household electricity price, CO2/capita, and 8 World Bank socioeconomic indicators (GDP/capita, inflation, unemployment, Gini, etc.) for 167-170 countries. Live endpoint: https://aykutsp.github.io/world-infrastructure-data-hub/api/v1/countries.json. v1.1 adds 15-year historical time series with sparklines for CO2 and World Bank indicators.
why_useful: A global (not just US) retail gasoline price panel by country is directly relevant to ABNB's EMEA/LatAm/APAC regional consumer-fuel-cost proxies and could feed a cross-region driving-cost index alongside FX and inflation, touching both gap #7 (regional travel volume/consumer strength) and the road-travel theme; free, no-key, machine-readable JSON API refreshed daily.
time_coverage: current snapshot daily; v1.1 adds historical time series (up to 15 years) for CO2/World Bank fields (fuel price history not stated as historized)
license: MIT (code) / CC BY 4.0 and ODbL for underlying data sources
themes: Road travel and fuel: gas prices (EIA, AAA), vehicle miles travelled, holiday driving, toll data
why_all: A global (not just US) retail gasoline price panel by country is directly relevant to ABNB's EMEA/LatAm/APAC regional consumer-fuel-cost proxies and could feed a cross-region driving-cost index alongside FX and inflation, touching both gap #7 (regional travel volume/consumer strength) and the road-travel theme; free, no-key, machine-readable JSON API refreshed daily.

name: AllRates-Today/ecb-exchange-rate
what_it_holds: Zero-dependency Node.js/TypeScript client wrapping the ECB's official daily reference-rate feed: ~41 currencies vs EUR, full history back to 1999 (ECB's own published range). No data files committed beyond the client code; it re-fetches from ECB's public XML feed on demand.
why_useful: One-command pull for daily EUR cross-rates since 1999 covering all of ABNB's EMEA-relevant currencies (GBP, and via cross-rates most others); useful for building our own point-in-time FX vintage register (rule #2 in our own CLAUDE.md) since ECB rates are date-stamped at source.
duplicate_of_holding: We already hold FX schedules per CONTEXT.md; this is a possibly-longer/cleaner daily-since-1999 acquisition method worth flagging per the 'better/longer/older' rule.
themes: FX and purchasing power: exchange-rate history (ECB, BIS, FRED), broad-dollar indices, PPP/Big Mac, tourist affordability indices, company FX-exposure tooling
why_all: One-command pull for daily EUR cross-rates since 1999 covering all of ABNB's EMEA-relevant currencies (GBP, and via cross-rates most others); useful for building our own point-in-time FX vintage register (rule #2 in our own CLAUDE.md) since ECB rates are date-stamped at source.
